key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive crystal plasticity simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures while balancing competing spall and yield strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, data-driven microstructure design for structural metals, cutting optimization cost by orders of magnitude while retaining full-field response fidelity needed for engineering decisions.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline copper microstructures to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Derivative-free optimization searches stochastic microstructure space using the surrogate as the objective evaluator.
A distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on MMD flags when designs drift beyond the surrogate’s training distribution.
evidence_signal: Across multiple design cases, CPFE validation showed less than 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization reduced cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude versus direct CPFE optimization.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying within the surrogate’s distribution-consistent region; outside it, predictions may degrade and require high-fidelity revalidation.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
